question.text:
If the function $f(x)$, defined below, is continuous on the interval $[0,8]$, then
$f(x)=\left\{\begin{array}{cc}x^2+a x+b & , 0 \leq x \lt 2 \\ 3 x+2, & 2 \leq x \leq 4 \\ 2 a x+5 b, & 4 \lt x \leq 8\end{array}\right.$

solution.text:
Here, $f(x)$ is continuous on the interval $[0,8]$.
So it will also be continuous on 2 and 4.
At $x=2$,
$\lim _{x \rightarrow 2^{-}} f(x)=\lim _{x \rightarrow 2^{+}} f(x)$
$\lim _{x \rightarrow 2^{-}}\left(x^2+\mathrm{ax}+\mathrm{b}\right)=\lim _{x \rightarrow 2^{+}}(3 x+2)$
$4+2 a+b=3(2)+2$
$\therefore 2 a+b=4$    ...(i)
At $x=4$
$\lim _{x \rightarrow 4^{-}} f(x)=\lim _{x \rightarrow 4^{+}} f(x)$
$\lim _{x \rightarrow 4^{-}}(3 x+2)=\lim _{x \rightarrow 4^{+}} 2 a x+5 b$
$3(4)+2=2 a(4)+5 b$
$\therefore 8 a+5 b=14$  .......(ii)
On solving Eqs. (i) and (ii), we get
$a=3$ and $b=-2$.

question.text: The mean of n items is X . If the first item is increased by 1 , second by 2 and so on, the new mean is :

solution.text:
Let the items be $\mathrm{a}_1, \mathrm{a}_2, \ldots \ldots . ., \mathrm{a}_{\mathrm{n}}$
then $\bar{X}=\frac{a_1+a_2+\ldots \ldots .+a_n}{n}$
Now, according to the given condition:
$\bar{X}=\frac{\left(a_1+1\right)+\left(a_2+2\right)+\ldots \ldots \ldots+\left(a_n+n\right)}{n}$
$=\overline{\mathrm{X}}+\frac{1+2+3+\ldots \ldots \ldots+n}{n}=\bar{X}+\frac{n(n+1)}{2 n}$
(using sum of n natural nos.)
$=\overline{\mathrm{X}}+\frac{\mathrm{n}+1}{2}$.

question.text: The mean of five observations is $4$ and their variance is $5.2$. If three of these observations are $1$,$2$ and $6$ , then the other two are

solution.text:
Let the two unknown items be $x$ and $y$. Then,
$\operatorname{Mean}=4 \Rightarrow \frac{1+2+6+x+y}{5}=4$
$\Rightarrow \quad x+y=11\dots(i)$
and variance $=5.2$
$\Rightarrow \frac{1^2+2^2+6^2+x^2+y^2}{5}-(\text { mean })^2=5.2$
$\Rightarrow \quad 41+x^2+y^2=5(5.2+16)$
$\begin{array}{ll}\Rightarrow & 41+x^2+y^2=106 \\ \Rightarrow & x^2+y^2=65\end{array}$
On solving Eqs. (i) and (ii), we get
$x=4, y=7 \text { or } x=7, y=4$

question.text: Mean of 25 observations was found to be 78.4. But later on it was found that 96 was misread 69 . The correct mean is

solution.text:
Mean \(\bar{x}=\frac{\sum x}{n}\) or \(\Sigma x=n \bar{x}\)
\(\Sigma \mathrm{x}=25 \times 78.4=1960\)
But this \(\Sigma \mathrm{x}\) is incorrect as 96 was misread as 69 .
\(\begin{aligned}
& \therefore \text { correct } \Sigma \mathrm{x}=1960+(96-69)=1987 \\
& \therefore \text { correct mean }=\frac{1987}{25}=79.48
\end{aligned}\)

question.text: Find the mean deviation about the mean for the data $4,7,8,9,10,12,13,17$

solution.text:
Arithmetic mean $\bar{x}$ of $4,7,8,9,10,12,13$, 17 is
$\bar{x}=$ $\frac{4+7+8+9+10+12+13+17}{8}=\frac{80}{8}=10$
$\Sigma\left|x_i-\bar{x}\right|=6+3+2+1+0+2+3+7=24$
$\therefore$ Mean deviation about mean
$=\text { M.D. }(\bar{x})=\frac{\sum\left|x_i-\bar{x}\right|}{n}=\frac{24}{8}=3$

question.text: If the variance of the data $2,3,5,8,12$ is $\sigma^2$ and the mean deviation from the median for this data is M , then $\sigma^2-\mathrm{M}=$

solution.text:
Observations : $2,3,5,8,12$
Mean $=\frac{2+3+5+8+12}{5}=6$
$\therefore \sigma^2=13.2$
Median $=5=m$
$\therefore \quad$ Mean deviation about median
$\Rightarrow \quad \frac{\Sigma\left|x_i-m\right|}{n}=\frac{3+2+0+3+7}{5}=3$
$M=3 \Rightarrow \sigma^2-M=13.2-3=10.2$

question.text: The variance of 20 observations is 5 . If each observation is multiplied by 2 , then the new variance of the resulting observation is

solution.text:
Let the observations be $x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_{20}$ and $\bar{x}$ be their mean. Given that, variance $=5$ and $n=$ 20. We know that,
Variance $\left(\sigma^2\right)=\frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^{20}\left(x_i-\bar{x}\right)^2$
i.e. $5=\frac{1}{20} \sum_{i=1}^{20}\left(x_i-\bar{x}\right)^2$
or $\sum_{i=1}^{20}\left(x_i-\bar{x}\right)^2=100$     .....(i)
If each observation is multiplied by 2 and the new resulting observations are $y_i$, then
$y_i=2 x_i$ i.e., $x_i=\frac{1}{2} y_i$
Therefore,
$\overline{\mathrm{y}}=\frac{1}{\mathrm{n}} \sum_{\mathrm{i}=1}^{20} \mathrm{y}_{\mathrm{i}}=\frac{1}{20} \sum_{\mathrm{i}=1}^{20} 2 \mathrm{x}_{\mathrm{i}}=2 \cdot \frac{1}{20} \sum_{\mathrm{i}=1}^{20} \mathrm{x}_{\mathrm{i}}$
i.e., $\bar{y}=2 \bar{x}$ or $\bar{x}=\frac{1}{2} \bar{y}$.
On substituting the values of $x_i$ and $\bar{x}$ in eq. (i), we get
$\sum_{i=1}^{20}\left(\frac{1}{2} y_i-\frac{1}{2} \bar{y}\right)^2=100$
i.e., $\sum_{i=1}^{20}\left(y_i-\bar{y}\right)^2=400$
Thus, the variance of new observations
$=\frac{1}{20} \times 400=20=2^2 \times 5$.
